source_text:
Οἱ ἀργοὶ, τότε ἐργάται γεγόνασιν·

ἐργάζεται γὰρ νῦν ἥ ποτε ἀργὴ αὔτη Ἐκκλησία· ἐργάζεται ὁ χορὸς τῶν ἀποστόλων,
τῶν μαρτύρων, τῶν ἀσκητῶν, τῶν μοναζόντων, τῶν ἁγίων παρθένων, τῶν
ἐγκρατῶν, τῶν ἐν γάμῳ σεμνῷ· ἔλαβεν γὰρ αὔτη ἡ Ἐκκλησία τὸ ἒν δηνάριον ἀξίως.
∆ύναται γάρ τις ὀξέως ἐργαζόμενος, ἐν μιᾷ ὥρᾳ ἐνέγκαι ἔργον ὡς ἀπὸ πρωΐθεν
ἐργαζόμενος· ὁ λῃστὴς 77.1100 εἰς μίαν ὥραν ἤκουσεν τὸ, Σήμερον μετ' ἐμοῦ ἔσῃ ἐν
τῷ παραδείσῳ.
Ἀλλ' ἄκουσον τί φασιν ἐκεῖνοι· Ἡμεῖς οἱ βαστάσαντες τὸ βάρος καὶ τὸν
καύσωνα τῆς ἡμέρας· Ἀληθεύουσιν· οὐ γὰρ ἐν νόμῳ ἐβάστασαν τὸ βάρος τοῦ ζυγοῦ
τοῦ νόμου, ἀλλ' ἐγένοντο καὶ οὗτοι ἴσοι τούτων διὰ τὸ ἔργον· Ἑταῖρε, γὰρ, φησὶν,
οὐκ ἀδικῶ σε. Οὐκ ἀδικεῖ ὁ τῆς δικαιοσύνης κριτής· τὸ δὲ θέλω τούτῳ χαρίσασθαι ὡς
thought_title: The Idle Become Laborers and Are Paid Equally
orientation: The speaker now shows the once idle Church, that is the Gentiles, at work through its saints and lets the earlier laborers begin their complaint.
pass_a_gloss: The idle then have become laborers; for now this Church which was idle once works; works the band of the apostles, of the martyrs, of the ascetics, of those living as monks, of the holy virgins, of those with self control, of those in honorable marriage; for this Church has received the one denarius worthily. For one working swiftly is able in one hour to bring in work as one working from early morning; the thief in one hour heard the, Today with me you will be in paradise. But hear what those say; We who have borne the burden and the heat of the day; They speak truth; for not in law they bore the burden of the yoke of the law, but also these became equal to these through the work; Fellow for he says I do not wrong you. The judge of righteousness does not wrong; but the I wish to grant to this one as

choices.why: literal company of persons, not a singing choir here
keeps distinct class between virgins and married, avoids hyphen compound
adverb of manner for receiving the wage
direct address from the parable to the complaining laborer

bible_refs.note: Σήμερον μετ᾽ ἐμοῦ ἔσῃ ἐν τῷ παραδείσῳ
Ἡμεῖς οἱ βαστάσαντες τὸ βάρος καὶ τὸν καύσωνα τῆς ἡμέρας

pass_b_english: The idle have now become laborers. This Church was once idle, but she works now. The band of the apostles, martyrs, ascetics, those living as monks, holy virgins, those with self control, and those in honorable marriage is at work. This Church has received the one denarius worthily.
A worker who labors swiftly can present in one hour as much work as one who has labored since early morning. In a single hour the thief heard, “Today you will be with me in paradise” (Luke 23:43).

But hear what those earlier laborers say: “We bore the burden and the heat of the day” (Matthew 20:12). They speak the truth. For they did not bear under the law the burden of the yoke of the law, but these others became equal to them through the work. So the landowner says, “Fellow, I do you no wrong” (Matthew 20:13). The judge of righteousness does no wrong. He adds that he wishes to grant favor to this one.
notes: 77.1100 is a printed edition column marker, not source text, omitted from gloss
final clause breaks off at ὡς, gloss leaves it incomplete, no text invented
οὐ γὰρ ἐν νόμῳ as printed keeps negation in gloss though sense is strained

problems.quote: Under the law they bore the burden of the yoke of the law, yet these others became equal to them through their work.
problems.source_quote: οὐ γὰρ ἐν νόμῳ ἐβάστασαν τὸ βάρος τοῦ ζυγοῦ τοῦ νόμου, ἀλλ' ἐγένοντο καὶ οὗτοι ἴσοι τούτων διὰ τὸ ἔργον
problems.why: οὐ is dropped, so English affirms the burden under the law that the Greek denies, and turns ἀλλά into a mere contrast.
problems.fix: For they did not bear the burden of the law’s yoke under the law, but these too became equal to them through the work.
problems.ruling: Source has οὐ γὰρ ἐν νόμῳ ἐβάστασαν τὸ βάρος: they did NOT bear the law's yoke. English affirms the opposite by dropping the negation.

problems.quote: Cyril says they speak the truth.
problems.why: This is the homilist’s own verdict, not a narrator reporting what Cyril says.
problems.ruling: Ἀληθεύουσιν is the homilist's own verdict with no mention of Cyril. English adds a speaker and changes who is speaking.

problems.quote: The band of the apostles is at work — martyrs, ascetics, those living as monks, holy virgins, those with self control, and those in honorable marriage.
problems.source_quote: ἐργάζεται ὁ χορὸς τῶν ἀποστόλων, τῶν μαρτύρων, τῶν ἀσκητῶν, τῶν μοναζόντων, τῶν ἁγίων παρθένων, τῶν ἐγκρατῶν, τῶν ἐν γάμῳ σεμνῷ
problems.why: One chorus of parallel groups works; the dash makes the later groups rename the apostles.
problems.fix: The company of the apostles, martyrs, ascetics, monks, holy virgins, the self-controlled, and those in honorable marriage is at work.
problems.ruling: Source lists parallel genitive groups after ὁ χορὸς τῶν ἀποστόλων, τῶν μαρτύρων… The dash makes martyrs and the rest read as a rename of the apostles.

problems.quote: Cyril says they speak the truth.
problems.why: The English adds 'Cyril says', which the source does not have. This attributes the verdict to Cyril as a quoted speaker. In the source it is the author's own comment, with no separate attribution.
problems.ruling: Ἀληθεύουσιν is the author’s own “they speak truly”; English adds “Cyril says,” inventing a speaker the source lacks.

edits.old: The band of the apostles is at work — martyrs, ascetics, those living as monks, holy virgins, those with self control, and those in honorable marriage.
edits.new: The band of the apostles, martyrs, ascetics, those living as monks, holy virgins, those with self control, and those in honorable marriage is at work.

edits.old: Cyril says they speak the truth.
Under the law they bore the burden of the yoke of the law, yet these others became equal to them through their work.
edits.new: For they did not bear under the law the burden of the yoke of the law, but these others became equal to them through the work.

fixed: negation: restored οὐ ... ἀλλ' as 'did not bear ... but became equal' instead of affirming the burden.
speaker: removed narrator-report 'Cyril says'; Ἀληθεύουσιν is the homilist's own verdict: 'They speak the truth.'
mistranslation: changed dash-apposition to one parallel chorus-list with single 'is at work' for ὁ χορὸς τῶν ἀποστόλων, τῶν μαρτύρων ...
addition: removed added 'Cyril says' with no source in Ἀληθεύουσιν: 'They speak the truth.'
